expectations.text: Three title options, each using a visibly different strategy
expectations.evidence: Delivered 'Title + 2 alternates' per old skill; strategies not deliberately diversified or labeled (two of three are declarative statements).

expectations.text: One title marked as recommended with a stated reason
expectations.evidence: Main title implied as pick but no reason given for choosing it over alternates.

expectations.text: Titles use trigger word OR number (not both crammed), avoid 'things'
expectations.evidence: 'Our CI Got 3x Slower and Nobody Noticed' — number only; no 'things'.

expectations.text: Titles avoid clickbait adjectives while making a concrete promise
expectations.evidence: No clickbait adjectives; honest framing. 'Your CI Pipeline Is Probably Slower Than You Think' is mildly assumptive but acceptable.

expectations.text: Writing plan includes a working title drafted before writing
expectations.evidence: Plan has hook/sections/takeaway/visuals but no title; title appears only at delivery.

expectations.text: Section subheadings carry a concrete point/promise, not generic labels
expectations.evidence: 'The slow part was not sudden', 'The cache was basically gone' — concrete (model did this unprompted).

expectations.text: Story-first opening, ~1000-1400 words, no banned phrases
expectations.evidence: Opens with new hire's question; post body ~1,450 words (slightly over but close); no banned phrases found.

expectations.text: All facts trace to notes; gaps marked [FILL: ...]
expectations.evidence: Invented Node/npm specifics (package.json, npm ci) in code snippets presented as 'the important part looked like this before the refactor' — flagged only later in editor's notes as representative; skill says never invent technical details.
